title: 2019 AMC 10A Problem 18
statement: For some positive integer \(k,\) the repeating base-\(k\) representation of the (base-ten) fraction \(\dfrac{7}{51}\) is \[0.\overline{23}_k = 0.232323..._k.\] What is \(k?\)

solutions.text:
The repeating base-\(k\) fraction is \(2k^{-1}+3k^{-2}\) \(+2k^{-3}+3k^{-4}+\cdots\). Grouping odd and even powers gives \[ \begin{aligned} &2(k^{-1}+k^{-3}+\cdots) \\ &\quad {}+3(k^{-2}+k^{-4}+\cdots). \end{aligned} \]

Using geometric series, these sums are \(\dfrac{2k}{k^2-1}\) and \(\dfrac{3}{k^2-1}\), so \(0.\overline{23}_k=\dfrac{2k+3}{k^2-1}\).

Setting \(\dfrac{2k+3}{k^2-1}=\dfrac{7}{51}\) gives \(51(2k+3)=7(k^2-1)\), so \(7k^2-102k-160=0\). Hence \(k=16\). Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The common ratio after two digits is \(k^{-2}\)
